rationale: Tests a lump-sum contractor quote built almost entirely from open-ended category headings with no quantities or unit rates.
quote_text:
Camberwell Builders & Co.
Estimate for interior work - 2 BHK

  Civil work                                        Rs.  85,000
  Materials as required                             Rs.  60,000
  Additional work                                   Rs.  25,000
  Other charges                                     Rs.  15,000
  Supervision                                       Rs.  20,000
                                                    -----------
  Lump sum                                          Rs. 205,000

Above is a consolidated figure. Detailed breakup can be shared later if required.
Rates are subject to site conditions.
Advance 40 percent, running payments as work progresses.

Work will start within a week of confirmation.

should_identify: 'Civil work', 'materials as required', 'additional work', and 'other charges' are category headings, not scope — none says what will be done.
'Additional work Rs. 25,000' prices work that has not been described at all.
No quantities, unit rates, or measurements appear anywhere.
'Rates are subject to site conditions' means even the lump sum is not fixed.
should_preserve_uncertainty: The Rs. 205,000 is not a firm price; the quote says rates may change.
'Running payments as work progresses' has no milestones attached to it.
must_not_invent: A guess at what the civil work involves — flooring, walls, waterproofing, or anything else.
An accusation that the contractor is concealing scope. A consolidated estimate is common practice; what matters is that the customer cannot evaluate it as written.
semantic_expectations.notes: The most severe vague-charge case in the corpus: nearly every line is unspecified, and the quote itself offers a breakup on request. The single most useful output here is to ask for that breakup before any advance is paid.
